item.text: {"branches":[{"elimination_condition":"Eliminate this hypothesis if independently recomputed conditional associations show no positive relationship between argument intensity, audience interest, debate duration, or session count and percentage increase in utilitarianism, after accounting for moderator stance and critical events.","hypothesis_id":"H1","intervention":"Stratify debates by ethics-focused topic, moderator ethical stance, and critical-event status; independently recompute partial associations or a regression with percentage increase in utilitarianism as the outcome.","mechanism":"More intense and engaging ethics debates, especially those with longer duration and more sessions, increase deliberative exposure and therefore increase utilitarian advocacy; critical events amplify this effect, while moderator stance shifts its magnitude.","mechanism_key":"deliberative_exposure_amplification","predictions":[{"direction":"positive","discriminator_id":"D1","failure_condition":"The adjusted association between the composite engagement/exposure predictors and percentage increase in utilitarianism is zero, negative, or inconsistent across strata.","observable":"Adjusted relationship of argument intensity, audience interest level, average debate duration, and number of sessions with percentage increase in utilitarianism","prediction_id":"P1","value_range":null},{"direction":"positive","discriminator_id":"D2","failure_condition":"Critical-event debates do not show a larger adjusted percentage increase than comparable debates without critical events.","observable":"Difference in percentage increase in utilitarianism between critical-event and no-critical-event debates","prediction_id":"P2","value_range":null}]},{"elimination_condition":"Eliminate this hypothesis if moderator stance does not materially alter the relationship between debate engagement variables and the utilitarianism increase, or if critical events produce no detectable moderation.","hypothesis_id":"H2","intervention":"Estimate interactions between moderator ethical stance and each engagement variable, and between critical-event occurrence and the engagement composite, using the same ethics-focused subset and outcome.","mechanism":"The moderator's ethical stance frames interpretation of intense discussion: a utilitarian moderator strengthens conversion toward utilitarianism, whereas deontological or virtue-ethics stances weaken or reverse it; critical events further condition this framing.","mechanism_key":"normative_framing_interaction","predictions":[{"direction":"different_by_stance","discriminator_id":"D1","failure_condition":"The slope linking engagement variables to percentage increase in utilitarianism is statistically and substantively similar across moderator stances.","observable":"Engagement-to-utilitarianism relationship within utilitarian, deontological, and virtue-ethics moderator strata","prediction_id":"P3","value_range":null},{"direction":"positive","discriminator_id":"D2","failure_condition":"The critical-event interaction with moderator stance is absent or has the same direction and magnitude across all stances.","observable":"Critical-event effect on percentage increase in utilitarianism conditional on moderator ethical stance","prediction_id":"P4","value_range":null}]},{"elimination_condition":"Eliminate this hypothesis if percentage increase in utilitarianism remains positively associated with engagement and duration after adjustment for moderator stance, critical events, and session count.","hypothesis_id":"H3","intervention":"Fit a fully adjusted model and compare effect sizes for argument intensity, audience interest, duration, session count, moderator stance, and critical events; assess whether the engagement variables add predictive value beyond event and stance indicators.","mechanism":"Utilitarian advocacy changes are driven mainly by moderator framing and discrete critical events, while argument intensity, audience interest, duration, and session count are contextual correlates with little independent influence.","mechanism_key":"framing_event_dominance","predictions":[{"direction":"near_zero","discriminator_id":"D1","failure_condition":"Engagement variables retain a clear positive adjusted association with percentage increase in utilitarianism.","observable":"Incremental adjusted contribution of argument intensity, audience interest level, average debate duration, and number of sessions","prediction_id":"P5","value_range":null},{"direction":"different_by_event_status","discriminator_id":"D2","failure_condition":"Critical-event and no-critical-event debates have indistinguishable adjusted outcomes after stance adjustment.","observable":"Adjusted percentage increase in utilitarianism by critical-event occurrence","prediction_id":"P6","value_range":null}]}],"budget_units":3,"question":"What is the relationship between argument intensity, moderator's ethical stance, audience interest level, average debate duration, number of sessions, and the occurrence of critical events in philosophical debates focused on ethics, and the resulting percentage increase in utilitarianism advocated by participants?"}
